subject.title: [Feature Request] Telegram Channel: Support Thread Binding for Subagent Sessions

question: Should Telegram expose child-topic native subagent session spawning now, and should that be implemented through the core session-binding adapter capability rather than deprecated `subagent_spawning` hooks?
rationale: Current main partially supports Telegram current-conversation binding, but child-topic spawning changes visible Telegram topic creation, plugin capability/API shape, and session/message routing defaults.

options.title: Review or replace the active Telegram PR
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/82023 as the design input, require a rebase and ownership fixes, and validate the final head with live Telegram proof.

options.title: Defer child-topic spawning
options.body: Keep current-conversation Telegram binding only until maintainers settle the visibility and API model for child topics.

options.title: Reject Telegram child-topic subagent spawning
options.body: Close this direction and associated candidate work if maintainers decide internal subagent runs should not create Telegram topics.

recommendation.title: Review or replace the active Telegram PR
recommendation.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/82023 as the design input, require a rebase and ownership fixes, and validate the final head with live Telegram proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved choice sits on the core thread-binding refactor and plugin API direction that steipete most directly authored.
